text:
alex: noticing a sharp p95 east-west spike across GPU nodes in rack-7 during the noon batch window. started ~12:13, lasted ~6m. looks correlated with high batch concurrency. :eyes:

maria: which metric? p95 token latency or RPC? link?

alex: p95 gen latency (token path) and grpc RTT between gnode-72/73. dash: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/gnode-latency. baseline ~40ms, spiked to 600-900ms.

chen: saw something similar last month — usually an RDMA path issue or qpair saturation when we push >200 concurrent batching flows. can you paste mlx logs?

alex: grabbing logs now. short snip from gnode-73 dmesg:```
[Dec 14 12:14:21] mlx5_core 0000:82:00.1: EQ timeout, resetting device
[Dec 14 12:14:21] psm2: connection to peer 10.2.72.73 failed: timeout
[Dec 14 12:14:23] mlx5_core 0000:82:00.1: firmware recovered
[Dec 14 12:14:24] rdma_cm: connection error -113
```

sam: ethtool/ibv state from the same host:```
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
... tso: on gso: on gro: on
# ibv_devinfo -v
device: mlx5_0
max_qp: 16384
ports: 1
state: ACTIVE
```

maria: any config changes around 12:10? deploy-bot, did a config push?

deploy-bot: New commit deployed to infra/topo at 2024-12-14T12:09:58Z by sam: "ecmp-hash-tweak for better rack spreading" (commit 9a7f).

chen: hm ecmp/hash changes + bursty batching = different flow spread, can create hot-paths where some NICs/qps get overloaded while others idle. combined with an intermittent mlx firmware bug that produces EQ timeouts, results in path oscillation.

alex: we also saw a pattern: when the path resets, many batch requests retransmit in short window -> momentary fanout surge. that aligns with p95 spikes.

sam: i rolled the topo change back at 12:18 as a quick mitigation (reverted commit 9a7f). monitoring now.

maria: any quick mitigation beyond rollback? can we throttle batch window or route heavy batch traffic to dedicated pool? might be faster than full node reboot.

chen: short-term: reduce max_concurrent_batches per node by 30% (scheduler tweak) and enable fallback to CPU-batched path for non-critical traffic. medium: add per-pair qpair limits and tune ECMP to preserve locality for high-throughput flows.

alex: implementing scheduler cap now (patching batch-controller). pinging once done.

sam: after rollback + scheduler cap p95 dropped back to ~85ms at 12:27. still watching. :thumbsup:

maria: good. create an incident note and add runbook steps: detection alerts for mlx EQ timeouts, and playbook to revert topo changes and cap batch concurrency. chen can you draft?

chen: will do. i also want to capture full tcpdump/ibtrace of next event and open a vendor ticket with Mellanox (include firmware version and dmesg).

alex: added short logs to the incident. timeline: 12:09 topo change -> 12:13 batch spike -> 12:18 rollback -> 12:27 recovery.

maria: awesome. assign to infra oncall for follow-up and schedule a postmortem. thanks all.

alex: thanks — let's also add a perf regression test that simulates batch fanout plus ECMP churn. helps catch this before deploy. :+1:
